answer: The 'AI system lifecycle' refers to the typical phases that an AI system undergoes, which include planning and design; collecting and processing data; building model(s) and/or adapting existing model(s) to specific tasks; testing, evaluating, verifying, and validating; making the system available for use/deploying; operating and monitoring; and retiring/decommissioning. These phases often take place in an iterative manner and are not necessarily sequential. The decision to retire an AI system from operation may occur at any point during the operation and monitoring phase.
